channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula pede, e equipe econômica pode barrar quem quer refinanciar dívidas de apostar em bets
item.description: President Lula urged the economic team to restrict the use of online betting platforms (bets). In response, the Ministry of Finance proposed banning individuals enrolled in the new debt refinancing program from placing bets until their debts are paid. The government also considers using FGTS funds to pay debts with limits, consolidating credit card, overdraft, and personal loan debts with interest discounts ranging from 30% to 90%.

item.title: RJ: STF decide se eleição para mandato-tampão será direta ou indireta
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court is set to rule on Wednesday whether the interim gubernatorial election in Rio de Janeiro will be direct or indirect, following the TSE’s conviction and resignation of former governor Cláudio Castro. The PSD advocates for a popular vote, while the state’s succession line is depleted due to resignations and removals, leaving the President of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice as acting governor pending the STF’s decision.

item.title: O imprevisível julgamento do STF sobre as eleições no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The STF will rule this Wednesday on whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election will be direct or indirect, with ministers split 5-4 in favor of direct vote. Court President Edson Fachin holds the tie-breaking vote. The state faces political chaos due to resignations, arrests, and mandates revoked over corruption, leaving the Executive under interim leadership of the TJRJ president since March.

item.title: Bolsas europeias têm alta próxima a 5% com trégua entre EUA e Irã
item.description: European stock markets rose nearly 5% following a 14-day ceasefire between the U.S., Iran, and Israel, which reopened the Strait of Hormuz and eased geopolitical tensions. Brent crude oil dropped over 14%, signaling expectations of restored global energy flows. The Brazilian government announced measures to counter the domestic impact of prior fuel price spikes.

item.title: Áudio: Sancionada lei que garante acesso à imonuterapia no SUS
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.379/2026, expanding access to immunotherapy within the Unified Health System (SUS). The measure aims to guarantee advanced treatment for certain types of cancer, which specialists consider one of the greatest advances in oncology over the past 15 years. The law marks a significant step in broadening access to high-cost therapies in the public health system.

item.title: Petróleo cai até US$ 17,6 depois de cessar-fogo no Oriente Médio
item.description: Brent crude fell as low as $17.55 following the announcement of a ceasefire between the U.S., Israel, and Iran, with the barrel trading at $93.8, down 14.18%. The 14-day truce includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of global oil flows, easing global inflationary pressures. The Brazilian government announced measures to mitigate rising diesel, cooking gas, and aviation kerosene prices amid market volatility.

item.title: O colégio eleitoral onde Lula tem mais que o dobro de votos que Flávio, segundo pesquisa
item.description: In Pernambuco, Lula leads with 56% of voting intentions in the first round, more than double Flávio Bolsonaro's 25%, according to a Real Time Big Data poll. In a potential runoff, Lula's advantage grows to 59% against Bolsonaro's 32%, indicating strong favoritism for re-election in the state. The survey, with a 2 pp margin of error, interviewed 1,600 voters between April 7 and 8, 2026.

item.title: Luisa Mell contra Janja
item.description: Animal rights activist Luisa Mell criticized First Lady Janja for posting a video in which she cooks paca, a wild game meat, for President Lula on Easter Sunday, claiming she heard Janja say it was game meat. Mell, known for her advocacy for animal rights, deemed the act inappropriate and provocative.

item.title: Dividido, STF decide hoje se o Rio terá duas eleições diretas para governador este ano
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) will decide today whether Rio de Janeiro will hold two direct gubernatorial elections in 2026, due to the need to define rules for the temporary mandate resulting from the current governor's resignation. The decision is seen as pivotal for the state's political stability and could significantly influence the national electoral landscape. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: PT usa rap para relembrar aniversário de 8 anos da prisão de Lula
item.description: On April 7, 2026, the PT released a rap to mark the 8th anniversary of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's imprisonment, which began on April 7, 2018, following a second-instance conviction in the Guarujá triplex case. The song celebrates his return to power, references the 2021 Supreme Court ruling that annulled his convictions due to jurisdictional bias and judge Sergio Moro's partiality, and highlights how that decision restored his political rights, enabling his 2022 electoral victory. Lula is portrayed as resilient and triumphant over adversity.

item.title: Guerra mostra debilidade da economia no terceiro governo Lula
item.description: The Middle East war is slowing global economic growth, with the OECD projecting a 25% rise in oil and gas prices and higher interest rates, which should reduce Brazil’s GDP growth to 1.5% in 2026, down from 2.5% in 2025. This economic weakness in Lula’s third term — averaging 2.6% growth over four years — reinforces the perception of a long-standing low-growth trap and may be exploited in the 2026 electoral campaign.

item.title: Lula recebe 2º volume de biografia, escrita por Fernando Morais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received the second volume of his biography, written by Fernando Morais, at the Palácio do Planalto on April 7, 2026. The book covers the final years of the military dictatorship through Lula's 2002 election victory, based on the author's direct and frequent access to Lula since 2011. The third and final volume has no set publication date.

item.title: Lula tem 40,4% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 37%, em cenário de 1º turno, mostra pesquisa Meio/Ideia
item.description: Lula has 40.4% of voting intentions and Flávio Bolsonaro 37%, according to the Meio/Ideia poll, with a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points, indicating a technical tie. The poll was released on Wednesday, January 8.

item.title: 'Tentando sobreviver': a explicação do deputado que passou por quatro partidos em um mês
item.description: Paraná deputy Nelsinho Padovani changed parties four times in one month, moving from União Brasil to PL, then Republicanos, and finally to PP, describing it as a 'political accommodation' to secure a better position on the major ticket. He denies the move was related to electoral funds and says he is not running for re-election, seeking only a more comfortable environment to operate. Padovani also commented on Ratinho Junior’s withdrawal from the presidential race, predicting Flávio Bolsonaro will win 80% of the vote in Paraná and stating he will wait for his group’s decision before endorsing a gubernatorial candidate.

item.title: Meio/Ideia: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam tecnicamente no 1º e no 2º turno
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied in both the first and second rounds according to the Meio/Ideia poll, with a 2.5-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula has 40.4% and Flávio 37%; in the second, Flávio leads at 45.8% versus Lula’s 45.5%. Government approval has stabilized, with 31.4% rating it 'terrible,' and 51.4% of voters still undecided.

item.title: Câmara aprova regras para transição de governo após eleições
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill establishing minimum rules for the post-election government transition, requiring the outgoing administration to facilitate access to information, facilities, and technical support for the incoming team, under administrative sanctions and fines. The proposal also increases penalties by one-third for deliberate data withholding, damage to public property, intimidation of officials, or causing irreparable harm, and mandates that the transition team be formed within 72 hours in a parity-based composition, without pay except for public servants retaining their existing compensation.

item.title: STF decide se ‘mandato-tampão’ no Rio terá eleição direta ou indireta
item.description: The STF is deciding whether the interim governorship of Rio de Janeiro will be filled by direct popular vote or indirect vote by state legislators, following the conviction and resignation of Cláudio Castro. The PSD advocates for direct elections, while the TSE had initially ruled for indirect voting due to Castro's ineligibility. The outcome will determine who leads the state until the end of 2026, when the elected governor from the October 2026 vote will take office in January 2027.

item.title: 42,5% dizem que reunir poder no Judiciário é maior ameaça à democracia
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll released on April 8, 2026, shows 42.5% of Brazilian voters view the concentration of power in the Judiciary as the greatest threat to democracy, surpassing corruption (16.5%), polarization (13%), disinformation (9.7%), and foreign influence (9.1%). Only 4.3% believe democracy is not under threat. The survey of 1,500 respondents conducted from April 3–7 has a 2.5-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Apesar de denúncia em 2020, Flávio faz as pazes com Paulo Marinho
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has reconciled with Paulo Marinho, a former Bolsonaro ally and his Senate substitute, after a 2020 rift triggered by Marinho's allegation that Flávio received privileged information about Operation Furna de Onça. The rapprochement, initiated in 2024, was affirmed by André Marinho, Novo party pre-candidate for Rio governor, who praised Flávio's conciliatory stance and noted that Flávio and his father are '101%' aligned.

item.title: Flávio tem 45,8% e Lula 45,5% no 2º turno, diz Meio/Ideia
item.description: Meio/Ideia poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 45.8% and Lula (PT) at 45.5% in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, technically tied within a 2.5-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula leads with 40.4% versus Flávio’s 37.0%. The survey, registered with TSE as BR-00605/2026, interviewed 1,500 people from April 3–7, 2026, with 95% confidence and a cost of R$27,600, funded by Canal Meio.

item.title: 51,5% são contra Lula continuar no governo após 2026, diz Meio/Ideia
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll shows 51.5% of Brazilian voters oppose Lula’s re-election in 2026, while 45% support a fourth term. 3.5% were undecided. The survey, conducted April 3–7, 2026 with 1,500 respondents, has a 2.5-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Meio/Ideia: 28% defendem interferência estrangeira nas eleições
item.description: A Meio/Ideia survey released on April 8, 2026, shows that 52% of Brazilians believe elections should be decided solely by citizens, rejecting foreign interference. Meanwhile, 28% consider it legitimate to seek support from foreign governments to ensure electoral fairness, and 18.1% say they need more information. The poll, conducted from April 3–7 with 1,500 respondents, has a 2.5-point margin of error and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Governo Lula à deriva nas relações com o Congresso
item.description: Minister Gleisi Hoffmann resigned from the Ministry of Institutional Relations, as anticipated for months, amid growing tensions between the Lula government and Congress. Her departure reflects difficulties in political articulation and managing essential alliances for advancing government agendas. The episode reinforces the perception of a government adrift in an increasingly challenging and fragmented legislative environment.

item.title: Com eleição no radar, a 'turma do amor' turbina produção de narrativas
item.description: As the 2026 elections approach, rising government disapproval and declining popularity of President Lula have prompted the government and PT's narrative production units to operate at 24/7 capacity. The so-called 'turma do amor' — a term referring to Lula's close allies — is intensifying efforts to counter growing rejection and stabilize the government's image amid an unfavorable electoral landscape.

item.title: STF julga eleição no Rio em ação que pode atrapalhar palanque de Flávio
item.description: The STF begins today the judgment of an action that could define the future of politics in Rio de Janeiro, potentially weakening Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign in the state. Rio has the third-largest electorate in the country and is considered the birthplace of bolsonarism, making the outcome relevant for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Ideia: Endividamento puxa Lula para baixo; voto em Flávio ainda é volátil
item.description: The Meio/Ideia poll highlights that household debt is acting as an anchor on President Lula’s popularity, hindering his electoral recovery. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro, while a prominent right-wing figure, has not yet solidified his vote, as the entry of new right-wing candidates creates volatility in his support base.

item.title: O STF contra si mesmo
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) has seen its institutional authority erode due to internal failures, including expansive monocratic rulings, lack of transparency, and weakened collegiality, undermining its legitimacy despite its historical role in defending democracy.

item.title: STF decide como será a eleição no Rio com cassação de Castro; entenda a origem e o que está em jogo
item.description: The STF will decide whether to hold a direct or indirect election for Rio de Janeiro's governorship following the cassation of Cláudio Castro, due to concerns about overlapping with the October general elections. The TSE deems it logistically unfeasible to hold a direct election for the interim mandate so close to the 2026 elections, risking electoral overload. The ruling will be made in a hearing scheduled for April 8.

item.title: Por que Rio de Janeiro pode ter duas eleições para governador neste ano
item.description: Rio de Janeiro may hold two gubernatorial elections in 2026 after Governor Cláudio Castro resigned to avoid potential disqualification by the TSE, leaving no valid vice-governor following the resignation of Thiago Pampolha and the removal of Rodrigo Bacellar. The president of the TJ-RJ, Ricardo Couto de Castro, is serving as interim governor, but the STF will rule on April 8 whether a supplementary election will be held this year to determine who governs the state until the end of the term.

item.title: O apelo de aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro para Michelle se engajar na campanha
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro are frustrated with former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro's reluctance to engage in his presidential campaign, raising concerns about family support in the electoral race. Her resistance is seen as an obstacle to the PL party's efforts to consolidate backing for the senator's bid for the presidency.

item.title: Governo planeja novo programa para endividados: ‘enrolados’ contam como perderam o controle
item.description: The Lula government is finalizing discussions on a new debt renegotiation program, driven by high household indebtedness. One option under consideration is allowing the use of FGTS (severance fund) to pay off debts, as confirmed by Finance Minister Dario Durigan. The measure aims to ease income burden in an election year.

item.title: Bispo que presta assistência espiritual a Bolsonaro defende indicação de Jorge Messias ao STF: 'Cristão comprometido'
item.description: Bishop Robson Rodovalho, who provides spiritual assistance to jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, endorses the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, calling him 'extremely capable' and a 'committed Christian'. He acknowledges potential ideological differences with the right but stresses Messias’ openness to dialogue and faith-based guidance. The nomination still requires approval by the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ).

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro recorre à Justiça contra o X por 'campanha difamatória' que 'transcende liberdade de expressão'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro filed a lawsuit against X (formerly Twitter) to obtain user data from accounts allegedly spreading a defamatory campaign linking him to the 'rachadinha' scandal, militias, and criminal activity. He claims the posts exceed the bounds of free speech and constitute libel, slander, or defamation. Judge Marcello Pantoja Filho had previously granted part of the request in February, stating the content goes beyond legitimate political criticism.

item.title: Grupos de Paes e Ruas reforçam costuras para comando da Alerj enquanto aguardam decisão do STF sobre eleição
item.description: Allies of former mayor Eduardo Paes and deputy Douglas Ruas are intensifying negotiations for control of the Alerj while awaiting the STF’s decision on the state election. Paes’ camp seeks unity and has expanded its base through new affiliations, aiming for 23 votes to challenge Ruas’ PL, which needs 36 votes to lead the Assembly. The left is attempting to form a united front between PSD and PSOL, though the PSOL conditions its support on a candidate who openly defends President Lula.

item.title: Renúncia de Castro não 'surtiu efeitos pretendidos': por que a PGE defendeu eleição direta no Rio
item.description: The Electoral Attorney General's Office (PGE) argues that direct elections should be held for the caretaker governorship in Rio de Janeiro, asserting that the vacancy resulted from the TSE's conviction, not Claudio Castro's voluntary resignation. Vice-Prosecutor-General Alexandre Espinosa stated that diploma cassation by the TSE mandates new direct elections, per STF precedents from 2018. This position aligns with Minister Alexandre de Moraes' vote, which acknowledged the resignation but noted an abuse of purpose, and is expected to be supported by Ministers Flávio Dino, Gilmar Mendes, and Zanin, with the outcome hinging on the votes of Luiz Fux, Dias Toffoli, and Edson Fachin.

item.title: Janela Partidária: Podemos e PL saem vencedores; PDT e União perdem parte da bancada
item.description: The 2026 party window ended with significant gains for Podemos and PL, which increased their benches in the Chamber of Deputies. Podemos rose from 16 to 27 deputies, while PL grew from 87 to 97. Conversely, União Brasil and PDT suffered losses, reflecting strategic misalignments ahead of the October elections.

item.title: Partidos têm até esta quarta para indicar nomes para vaga de ministro no TCU, dizem líderes; entenda como funciona processo
item.description: Parties with representation in the Chamber of Deputies have until Wednesday (8) to nominate candidates for the TCU minister vacancy following the retirement of Aroldo Cedraz. The agreement between the government base and the PT to support Odair Cunha (PT-MG) remains in place, according to Chamber President Hugo Motta. Other parties have nominated Hugo Leal (PSD-RJ), Elmar Nascimento (União-BA), and Danilo Forte (PP-CE), while the PL is still deciding between Hélio Lopes (PL-RO) and Soraya Santos (PL-RJ).

item.title: Direita puxa fila para desgastar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Right-wing allies of Jair Bolsonaro are creating wear and tear on Flávio Bolsonaro, questioning his selection as successor to his ineligible father. Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos have launched pre-candidacies attacking Flávio from opposite flanks: Caiado for being too radical, and Renan for not being anti-system enough. The article notes that while the government and PT hesitate to confront Flávio, the internal right is generating the biggest obstacles to the Bolsonaro family succession project.

item.title: Aposentadoria especial para agentes de saúde abre precedente descabido
item.description: The proposal for special retirement for health agents is deemed unfounded by experts, as it could create a R$ 29.5 billion deficit in the pension system over ten years, significantly impacting both the federal government and municipalities. Federal authorities and city halls are mobilizing to block the PEC in Congress, despite its growing support in an election year. The actual impact may be higher, as current estimates do not account for the revision of already granted pensions or the legal risk of other careers demanding similar benefits through the courts.

item.title: STF julga nesta quarta ações que discutem a eleição para o governo do Rio; entenda
item.description: The STF is ruling this Wednesday (8) on two actions regarding the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election, deciding between a direct (popular vote) or indirect (state deputies' vote) model. The election is needed due to a power vacuum following the resignation of Cláudio Castro and the disqualifications of Rodrigo Bacellar and Thiago Pampolha, leaving the state under the interim leadership of TJ-RJ president Ricardo Couto until 2027.

item.title: PL e Missão ganham mais filiados em ano eleitoral; MDB perde mais e PT também recua
item.description: The PL and the newly formed Missão party gained the most members in Brazil between January and March 2026, with the PL adding 43,588 affiliates and Missão gaining 7,820, driven by electoral mobilization for 2026. The MDB led in losses with 5,062 fewer members, followed by PRD, PP, and PT, which lost 3,215 members despite retaining a substantial base. Despite these shifts, the parties with the largest losses remain among the country’s biggest political formations, according to TSE data.

item.title: STF julga se eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio será direta ou indireta; entenda o que está em jogo
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court is ruling this Wednesday on whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial interim election will be direct (popular vote) or indirect (chosen by state deputies), following the resignation and electoral conviction of former governor Cláudio Castro by the TSE. The core issue is whether Castro’s resignation was electorally motivated — due to his conviction — which would invalidate the state’s indirect election law and trigger the federal Electoral Code, mandating a popular vote. Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Cristiano Zanin, Flávio Dino, and Gilmar Mendes have already advocated for direct elections, while the votes of Luiz Fux, Dias Toffoli, and Edson Fachin are expected to be decisive.

item.title: Gestão Nunes cobra de governo Lula decisão técnica sobre fim de contrato da Enel
item.description: The Aneel's decision to initiate the caducity process of Enel's contract was met with relief by Mayor Ricardo Nunes' administration, which views the move as a necessary technical step to ensure energy service quality in São Paulo. Nunes urged the Lula government to make a technical and impartial decision on terminating the contract, emphasizing the need to avoid political interference in regulatory matters.

item.title: Julgamento sobre eleições é novo capítulo de 'fator STF' na política do RJ
item.description: The Federal Supreme Court (STF) ruled on Wednesday (8) on the definition of Rio de Janeiro’s future interim governor, reinforcing the court’s role in state politics. The decision is seen as another chapter in the so-called 'STF factor,' which has increasingly influenced governance in the state.

item.title: Rede Sustentabilidade diz receber com 'indignação e perplexidade' anúncio da permanência de Marina Silva na sigla
item.description: The national leadership of Rede Sustentabilidade expressed 'indignation and perplexity' over Marina Silva's decision to remain in the party, after she refused to dialogue with the directory and accused her allies of practicing lawfare. The party denies having suggested her departure and asserts that allied exits resulted from collective democratic decisions, not persecution. Marina justified her stay as a commitment to Lula and Haddad's re-election and the strengthening of Brazil's 'democratic biome'.

item.title: Governo de SP quer criar Olimpíadas do Conhecimento
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has submitted a bill to the state legislature to institutionalize the Knowledge Olympics as a permanent program of the State Education Secretariat. Since 2024, the initiative has engaged over 4 million students and awarded 500,000 medals to top performers. The move aims to solidify the program as a lasting public education policy.

item.title: Confirmada eleição suplementar para a Prefeitura de Cabedelo (PB) no dia 12 de abril
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the removal of Cabedelo’s mayor André Luís Almeida Coutinho (Avante) and vice-mayor Camila Holanda (PP) for abuse of economic and political power and vote-buying. The decision confirms the supplementary election scheduled for April 12, after the regional court declared Coutinho ineligible for eight years and fined him R$ 40 thousand. The TSE dismissed their appeals, stating due process was respected and the evidence — including Pix transfers, food baskets, WhatsApp chats, and witness testimonies — was substantial.

item.title: TSE reconhece candidaturas fictícias nas Eleições 2022 para deputado federal em São Paulo
item.description: The TSE recognized that the Pros party launched two fictitious female candidacies in the 2022 federal deputy elections in São Paulo, but upheld the party's Drap because the valid female candidacies reached 36.61%, exceeding the 30% gender quota. Mariana Cristina Pontes Papaiz and Andrea Cristina Pradella had their candidacies annulled and were declared ineligible for eight years, while the party's proportional slate was preserved.

item.title: Mendonça é sorteado relator de queixa-crime de Bolsonaro contra Janones no STF
item.description: Justice André Mendonça was drawn as rapporteur for the criminal complaint filed by former President Jair Bolsonaro’s defense against Congressman André Janones, who is accused of slander and defamation based on videos from March calling Bolsonaro a 'vagabond,' 'thief,' and 'pervert,' among other allegations. This is Bolsonaro’s second private criminal action against Janones in the STF; Mendonça, appointed by Bolsonaro, had previously voted to dismiss the first complaint in 2024, but the Court followed Justice Cármen Lúcia and ruled Janones should stand trial for insult.

item.title: Ex-ministro Moreira Franco lança livro sobre bastidores da política
item.description: Former minister Moreira Franco will launch his book 'Politics as Destiny: Paths and Detours of Redemocratization' this Wednesday (8) in Brasília, gathering leaders from MDB and the centrão. The work addresses the trajectory of Brazilian redemocratization, focusing on political backstage dynamics.
